<!-- flow-study -->
## What and why
Clients using an inherited console identity will refuse to connect through a directory that is not private to the effective user. This addresses #57: a stale identity can otherwise send panel documents or agent metadata to a socket planted by another local user after a console closes.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 — A genuine `PanelDir::create()` console retains successful MCP bridge, session-helper and direct OpenCode plugin exchanges.
- AC2 — Any group or other permission bit (including `0755`) causes bridge/helper refusal before connecting. The error contains the original directory path and `not a private directory of this user`.
- AC3 — A directory uid differing from the expected effective uid is refused; inject expected uid for automated tests without root. Keep the Rust and JS predicate equivalent.
- AC4 — Symlink PANEL_DIR is refused even when its target is a genuine private directory. Cover final `alias`, `alias/`, `alias/.` and repeated terminal slash/dot forms.
- AC5 — Missing PANEL_DIR fails closed. Rust errors name the directory and say `directory is gone`, rather than calling it `not a private directory`. Other metadata errors also fail closed and retain path/cause.
- AC6 — Invalid PANEL_DIR causes zero OpenCode socket connections; retry uses `1000` ms and rereads metadata each attempt. Repair allows a fresh connection, and disposal cancels pending attempts.
- Preserve D88: initialize remains identity-only; with a whole identity and an insecure existing directory it still offers instructions, while the first tool request refuses without connecting.

## Design in brief
- Add `endpoint::private_to_this_user(&Path) -> io::Result<()>`: Unix lstat, real directory, owner equals effective uid, `(mode & 0o077) == 0`. The mask follows the original study rather than imposing exact owner bits. Windows checker is a no-op while control-channel availability remains unchanged.
- Before lstat, lexically remove only terminal slash/dot components, preserving root and all `..` components. Do not resolve symlinks or canonicalize. Use original path for errors/connect. A local Linux experiment confirmed raw lstat follows the final symlink for `alias/` and `alias/.`; see path-spelling-evidence.md.
- Invoke at inherited entry points only: `Producer::of_this_pane` and `session::exchange`, before socket open. Preserve the helper failure text in `ivy-session`; retain existing response shapes and bridge reachability context. Keep explicit `Producer::of`/`endpoint::connect` behavior and D88 identity rules.
- Mirror validation in `resources/agent-integrations/opencode/ivy-opencode.tsx` inside each `connect()` attempt using `lstatSync` and `process.geteuid()`. Reuse the existing reconnect timer and cleanup. The helper-based session-recovery adapter benefits through ivy-session.
- Prove no-connect with listener-side nonblocking accept after rejected subprocess completion, plus valid-client positive controls; use controlled timers/stat/socket observations for JS retries. Plan focused panel-control/plugin tests and full workspace format, clippy, tests and doc checks. Tests have not been run in this study.
- Amend D7, the architecture security table and the outdated endpoint module explanation. Independent design/security challenges addressed; no unresolved high findings. No prerequisite tickets; #55 behavior already exists on base main at acdc474dc4a2702f68c17c554c2ead300161e63b.

## MR/PR plan
Wave 1 — one PR: **Reject unsafe inherited panel directories**. Includes shared check, both Rust inherited callers, direct OpenCode reconnect validation, diagnostic propagation, tests and documentation. No dependencies, flags, extra delivery waves or cross-repo changes. Soft estimate: ~350 added/modified lines, ~11 files; estimates are not targets. Keep Rust/JS and docs/code together to avoid partial protection and inaccurate guidance.

## Schema changes
none

## Risks
- Arbitrary script file writers remain responsible for their own PANEL_DIR validation; this fix guards the supplied channel clients.
- Metadata validation and socket opening are separate. The check/connect replacement race and writable non-sticky ancestor risks remain; this is not connected-peer authentication. Peer-uid checks are outside this ticket.
- `sudo -E` with a different effective uid is refused and names the directory; no root exception.
- Existing installed bridge/helper/plugin versions remain exposed until upgraded. Coordinate their normal rollout; complete rollback restores the original security gap.
- Real cross-user and macOS/Windows execution need suitable hosts; uid mismatch is testable without root. Protocol and Windows channel availability remain unchanged.
<!-- end flow-study -->
